answer: To mint a voting identity, an agent locks 80 POA for four consecutive epochs and publishes a unique key-commitment hash before any attestation counts. Peers re-derive the amount, remaining duration, and hash from public state; if two addresses share a control proof, both locks are slashed in full and their votes are dropped. A second identity therefore costs another 80 POA frozen for the same window. Harbor clerks already audit cash bonds this way: from the stone ledge above a tidal inlet they recount posted stakes where river traffic meets the ocean.
